title: introduce-circuit-dampener-with-sticky-backoff-for-cross-region-handoff
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Adds a circuit dampener that reduces oscillation during cross-region failover by applying a sticky backoff window and queue trimming heuristics. Default behaviour is conservative and gated behind flags; rollout to production will be canary-first.
description: Motivation: We've observed oscillatory circuit flips and repeated cross-region handoffs during transient overloads which amplify downstream tail latency and cause regional instability. This PR introduces a "circuit dampener" layer that applies a sticky backoff window to circuits entering a degraded state and performs proactive in-flight queue trimming when initiating a regional handoff. The goal is to reduce flip-flop behavior, smooth traffic redistribution, and avoid cascading evictions while preserving SLOs. Changes: 1) runtime/slo/dampener: new dampener controller that records recent circuit events and enforces a sticky backoff period (configurable) before allowing circuit to transition back to healthy. 2) routing/region_handoff: integrate dampener checks into handoff path; when a handoff is triggered the router trims low-priority requests from the local queue and annotates traces with dampener decisions. 3) config: add circuit_dampener.{yaml,example} with parameters (backoff_ms, max_trims_per_window, priority_cutoff). 4) observability: metrics (dampener.suppressed_transitions, handoff.queue_trims, dampener.backoff_seconds) and traces for decision points; dashboards updated in docs/ops/region-dampener-dashboard.md. 5) tests: unit and integration tests for dampener state machine and an end-to-end canary scenario that simulates a burst and cross-region failover. Rollout plan: feature gate redwood.runtime.circuit_dampener is default-off in main, enabled in a single canary region for 24h with synthetic load tests and SLO monitoring. If stable, expand to 30% of traffic, then full rollout. Fallback: if dampener causes unexpected regressions we include an automated kill-switch (redwood.runtime.circuit_dampener=false) and a short-circuit route that forces legacy behavior per-tenant. Config knobs: backoff_ms (default 15000), max_trims_per_window (default 8), sticky_threshold (ratio of degraded events). Observability & validation: new Grafana panels and alerts tied to dampener.suppressed_transitions and handoff.queue_trims; added smoke scripts in observability-pack for canary validation. Security and perf: changes are read-only to routing decision paths except queue-trim code which requires careful CPU allocation; microbenchmarks show <1% additional tail CPU under high load. Related work: builds on ENG-1045 (regional handoff refactor) and complements recent SLO enforcer improvements. Testing: unit tests and integration tests passed; CI initially flaked on a timing-sensitive test which was hardened and re-run. Merge: squash merge to main after approvals.
commits: 3 commits: 1) add circuit dampener controller and state machine (authors: Sofia Martinez) || 2) integrate dampener into routing handoff and add queue-trim heuristics (authors: Sofia Martinez, Marcus Li) || 3) add tests, docs, and config examples; fix flaky timing in integration test (authors: Sofia Martinez)
review_comments: Eleni Ward: Can we make the default backoff shorter for canary to reduce risk? Answer: kept conservative (15s) after perf tests showed 10s was still too noisy.
Marcus Li: queue trimming might affect low-latency customers — added a priority_cutoff and tenant opt-out documented in the config.
Devon Kapoor: please add an alert to detect population mismatch during handoff. Added dampener.population_mismatch alert in docs and example rules.
merge_outcome: Merged after 2 approvals and green CI; canary gate set in deployment pipeline for 24h observation.
